_meta.purpose: Companion to the OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 L1 starter pack: the failure modes the Level 1 verification requirements exist to prevent. frameworkTag 'ASVS', category 'Application Security'.
_meta.origin: Moved verbatim from the inline `asvsRiskTemplates` array in prisma/seed.ts (2026-11-08), so production receives it: prisma/seed.ts is never run on a deploy.
_meta.deliveredBy: scripts/seed-risk-templates.ts on every container start (scripts/entrypoint.sh), and prisma/seed.ts in dev, both through prisma/risk-template-fixtures.ts.

templates.title: Injection Vulnerability Exploited
templates.description: Untrusted input reaches an interpreter (SQL, OS command, LDAP, template) because it was not parameterized or validated, letting an attacker execute unintended commands.

templates.title: Broken Authentication
templates.description: Weak password handling, missing anti-automation, or poor recovery flows let an attacker take over user accounts.

templates.title: Broken Access Control
templates.description: Authorization is enforced only client-side or object references are not checked, so a user can reach data or actions outside their permission.

templates.title: Cross-Site Scripting
templates.description: User-supplied content is rendered without context-aware output encoding, allowing script execution in the browser of another user.

templates.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
templates.description: Sensitive data is transmitted or stored without adequate encryption, or leaks through caching, logs, or client-side storage.

templates.title: Security Misconfiguration
templates.description: Missing security headers, verbose errors, debug modes, or permissive CORS leave the application exposed in production.

templates.title: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
templates.description: A known-vulnerable dependency is exploited because components were not kept current or their integrity was not verified.

templates.title: Business Logic Abuse
templates.description: Workflow steps, timing, or quantity limits are not enforced server-side, letting an attacker automate or bypass business rules.
